subject: pharmacology
title: Serotonin, ergot alkaloids and antimigraine drugs

steps.tx: Serotonin (5-HT) acts through four receptor families: 5-HT1, 5-HT2, 5-HT3 and 5-HT4. All except 5-HT3 are **G protein coupled**. The 5-HT3 receptor is a **ligand gated cation channel**, and it mediates the emetic reflex. Know which receptor does what, because exam questions ask it directly. 5-HT1 receptors mostly act as autoreceptors that inhibit serotonin release.

steps.tx: Migraine is a throbbing, usually unilateral headache with nausea and light sensitivity. Sumatriptan is a **selective 5-HT1B/1D agonist** and is the drug of choice for aborting an acute attack. It is poorly absorbed orally, so the subcutaneous route acts faster. Triptans are **contraindicated in ischaemic heart disease**, because they cause coronary vasospasm.

steps.tx: Ergot alkaloids come from the fungus Claviceps purpurea. Ergotamine and dihydroergotamine abort acute attacks, while methysergide was used for prophylaxis. Ergots cause sustained vasoconstriction, so they are **contraindicated in ischaemic heart disease, peripheral vascular disease and pregnancy**. Ergotism from chronic use causes gangrene. Bromocriptine, an ergot derivative, is a D2 agonist for hyperprolactinaemia and Parkinsonism.

steps.tx: Prophylaxis is considered when attacks are more than two or three per month. **Propranolol** is the most commonly used agent. Flunarizine, topiramate, amitriptyline and valproate are also options. Drugs with intrinsic sympathomimetic activity, such as pindolol, are ineffective. Sumatriptan is never used for prophylaxis.

steps.tx: Newer antimigraine drugs include **CGRP pathway agents**. Erenumab is a monoclonal antibody against the CGRP receptor, and rimegepant and ubrogepant are oral CGRP antagonists. Lasmiditan is a 5-HT1F agonist that lacks vasoconstrictor action, so it suits patients with cardiovascular risk. Romosozumab is an osteoporosis drug and is not an antimigraine agent.

steps.tx: Know the serotonergic antagonists. **Ondansetron** is a 5-HT3 antagonist used for chemotherapy induced vomiting. **Ketanserin** is a selective 5-HT2 antagonist. **Methysergide** and **cyproheptadine** block 5-HT2 receptors and are used in carcinoid syndrome. Methysergide causes fibrosis, so it should not be given continuously beyond six months. Serotonin syndrome, from excess serotonergic drugs, causes agitation, tremor and hyperthermia.
